historical_references.reference:
Samiir ibn Jundub al-Ansari was a prominent companion of Prophet Muhammad (pbuh). He was known for his bravery and piety. During the battle of Badr, Samiir was the standard-bearer for the Muslim army and was instrumental in the victory. After the battle, when the Muslims were encamped, Samiir offered his prayer mat to the Prophet (pbuh) to pray on. This act of generosity and respect towards the Prophet (pbuh) is widely acknowledged in Islamic literature.
Time period: 624 AD - 632 AD
Context: Early Islamic history, Battle of Badr

Samiir al-Din Muhammad ibn Abd al-Wahhab was the founder of the Wahhabi movement in the 18th century. He was born in the central Arabian Peninsula and emphasized a return to the 'pure' form of Islam as practiced by the Prophet Muhammad (pbuh) and his companions. Samiir al-Din Muhammad rejected the veneration of saints and the building of tombs and mausoleums, and focused on the importance of personal devotion and the primary sources of Islamic law. He gained a large following and his teachings influenced the formation of the modern Saudi Arabian state.
Time period: 1703 AD - 1787 AD
Context: Islamic religious history, Founder of Wahhabi movement
